items.title: Elvis Presley IP Owners Sue Anthropic Over Allegations of Copyright Infringement

items.title: Reservoir hits Suno and Anthropic with copyright infringement lawsuits
items.summary: Reservoir Media is the latest music rightsholder taking aim at AI companies in the courts. It’s gone with a double-pronged attack, suing both Suno and Anthropic on the same day this week. The post is from Music Ally .

items.title: As UMG v. Suno Subpoenas Target the MLC, Multiple Investors, DistroKid, and Now Apple Music, Are Game-Changing Disclosures on the Horizon?
items.summary: As Suno fends off an ever-growing number of music industry copyright complaints, a raft of subpoena showdowns – including the AI platform’s own document and deposition demands – are now in full swing. Does that mean game-changing disclosures are on the horizon? Time will tell, though the current evidence suggests yes.…

items.summary: The big debate over whether or not AI training is fair use under US copyright law was taking place in court again yesterday, this time in the context of music, specifically lyrics, with the copyright legal battle between AI company Anthropic and the Universal, Concord and ABKCO music publishers

items.summary: As Anthropic prepares to go public, the lawsuits from the music industry keep on coming. Latest to sue the AI giant is Authentic Brands Group, owner of a number of IP rights relating to Elvis Presley. The post is from Music Ally .

tip.title: Voz clonada: el derecho en juego suele no ser el copyright
tip.body: Imitar la voz de un artista con IA rara vez es infracción de copyright de la canción; el reclamo típico va por derechos de imagen, voz y publicidad, que varían mucho entre jurisdicciones.

tip.title: Cloned vocals: copyright is usually not the issue
tip.body: Mimicking an artist's voice with AI is rarely a copyright infringement of the song itself; claims typically run through name, image, voice and publicity rights, which vary widely by jurisdiction.
